details:
**Rosa the Beautiful**
Rosa del Valle, famous for her green hair, dies in the novel's first chapter. She drinks poisoned brandy meant for her father, the Liberal Party Senate candidate Severo del Valle. She had been engaged to Esteban Trueba.

**Clara del Valle**
Rosa's clairvoyant younger sister, who foresaw Rosa's death and blames herself for predicting it. She falls silent for nine years afterward, then breaks her silence to announce she will marry Esteban Trueba, Rosa's former fiancé. She holds Friday sessions with the spiritualist Mora sisters around a three-legged table, against her father's wishes.

**Esteban Trueba**
The novel's patriarch and one of its narrators. He works in a mine to earn enough money to marry Rosa, then marries Clara after Rosa dies. He is violent and conservative, rapes peasant women including Pancha García, and dies in his granddaughter Alba's arms after writing his memoir.

**"Barrabás came to us by sea"**
The novel's opening line, describing the arrival of the huge dog Barrabás. Clara receives him after her Uncle Marcos dies. Barrabás is stabbed in the back and dies at Clara's engagement party; Esteban later has him made into a rug, and Clara faints on seeing it.

**Pedro Tercero García**
The son of the Tres Marías foreman, a revolutionary songwriter, Blanca Trueba's lover, and the father of Alba. When Esteban finds him with Blanca, he cuts off three of Pedro's fingers with an axe, and Pedro flees on horseback. Pedro and Blanca later escape the coup to Canada, where his songs about chickens and foxes are popular. Esteban later receives three fingers in the mail.

**Tres Marías**
The rural hacienda (estate) that Esteban rebuilds into a "model hacienda." It is the setting of his abuses of the peasants and of Blanca and Pedro Tercero's childhood romance. Its old man Pedro García rids the estate of an ant infestation and heals Esteban's broken bones after an earthquake.

**Count Jean de Satigny**
A French count who wants to start a chinchilla farm. He reveals Blanca's affair with Pedro Tercero, and Blanca is then forced to marry him. She leaves him after finding his pornographic photographs of their Indian servants.

**Alba Trueba**
Blanca's daughter and Esteban's granddaughter. She narrates the frame story, writing the family history while awaiting the birth of a child conceived by rape in a military prison. She joins student protests with Ana Díaz and is the lover of the revolutionary Miguel, who witnessed her birth from a closet. She is the last of four generations of women whose names mean "white" or "light": Nívea, Clara, Blanca, Alba.

**Tránsito Soto**
A prostitute whom Esteban meets at the Red Lantern brothel and lends money to. Years later, as a well-connected madam, she repays him by securing Alba's release from prison after the military coup.

**"Those who have always won will win again"**
The Conservative Party campaign slogan Esteban Trueba uses when he runs for the Senate. It contrasts with the earlier Liberal candidacy of Severo del Valle, which ends after the poisoning that kills Rosa.

**Clara's knocked-out teeth**
When Esteban learns of Blanca's affair, Clara defends her, and he strikes Clara, knocking out her front teeth. Clara never speaks to him again and moves out with Blanca.

**Nívea del Valle's head in a hatbox**
Clara's mother Nívea, a suffragette and mother of fifteen children, is decapitated in a car crash. Clara finds the head and keeps it in a hatbox under her bed, then goes into labor with the twins Jaime and Nicolás.

**Nicolás and the Institute of Union with Nothingness**
After returning from India, Clara's son Nicolás founds this spiritual institute and persuades his young niece Alba to shave her head. When he chants naked in front of the gates of Congress, Esteban has a heart attack. His brother Jaime, a doctor, performs an abortion for Nicolás's lover Amanda.

**Férula Trueba**
Esteban's devoted sister, whom he throws out of the house after finding her in bed with Clara. She curses him, saying his body and soul will shrivel and he will die like a dog.

**Uncle Marcos**
Clara's eccentric uncle, who courts his cousin by giving her a parrot with a foul vocabulary and vanishes in a homemade flying machine. After he dies, Clara inherits the dog Barrabás.
